1: # Pull-Request Adapter Boundary
2: 
3: ## Current scope
4: 
5: The owner has a version-1 internal, provider-neutral pull-request contract and a
6: Gitea Community implementation. A PR binding is a separate project capability
7: from remote hosting, issue tracking, and CI. Configuration of one does not
8: configure or authorize another. The owner stores at most one enabled PR binding
9: per project as immutable numbered revisions. Replacement and disable require the
10: expected current revision; earlier revisions remain readable for effects that
11: were already admitted. Each binding stores a Gitea instance ID, base URL,
12: repository owner/name and native repository ID, plus a reference to a named
13: systemd credential. The credential value is outside the binding and never
14: appears in API, CLI, or browser projections. The base URL accepts HTTPS or
15: loopback HTTP and rejects embedded credentials, queries, and fragments.
16: 
17: The owner API supports sanitized project-scoped binding list, configure,
18: disable, and probe operations under `/api/v1/settings/pull-requests`. Only the
19: local Unix bearer operator client can configure or disable a binding. The probe
20: authenticates the exact native repository ID and reads the pull-request list;
21: successful read access returns `partial/mutation_unverified`. It does not claim
22: draft creation, review, or merge permission. The `pr list`, `pr configure
23: --file`, `pr disable`, and `pr probe` owner CLI commands use those same routes.
24: Settings displays the sanitized current binding for the selected project. A
25: browser cannot configure or disable it.
26: 
27: An authenticated, project-scoped read at
28: `/api/v1/pull-requests/bindings/:bindingId/pulls/:nativeId` returns a bounded
29: PR observation. `pr inspect` uses that route. It contains the provider/instance/
30: native repository identity, PR number, exact head and base refs and commit
31: revisions, open/closed/merged and draft states, mergeability, supported merge
32: strategy, branch-protection required checks and approval count, advisory commit
33: statuses, attributed review decisions, discussion count, provider update time,
34: and provider URL when it has the configured origin. The Gitea API does not
35: expose a reliable queued-auto-merge read in this contract, so `queuedMerge` is
36: `unknown`; the owner never requests auto-merge. The update time is observation
37: metadata, not a write precondition. A PR with a different native repository ID
38: is rejected even when its owner/name looks similar.
39: 
40: The Gitea adapter reads the repository, PR, base-branch protection, combined
41: head status, and PR reviews. It calls no Issues or Actions route. Reads reject
42: redirects, use a ten-second deadline, and cap each JSON response at one million
43: bytes. Review and status collections are capped at fewer than 100 records; a
44: larger or incomplete collection fails closed. Review identity includes provider
45: review ID, actor ID, login and provider actor type, decision, reviewed head
46: commit, dismissal and staleness flags, and submission time. A comment or
47: reviewer request is not a Human approval. An unknown actor type and a review of
48: another head cannot authorize merge. The latest observed decision per Human
49: actor controls; a later dismissed or stale decision cannot leave an earlier
50: approval effective. Gitea review records carry a reviewed head commit but no
51: review-time base revision. The owner merge authority must bind its Human
52: decision to the current candidate base revision; provider approvals alone are
53: insufficient authority. Required status contexts come from
54: effective branch protection. Other commit statuses remain advisory and their
55: failure does not by itself block merge.
